subject: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-098.turn3.draft.md
summary: Turn 3 lands the warm-p50, image-version, label-source, storage-classification, and reversibility repairs. The five and only five D-006 startup quantities are operative, weekly image rolls cannot suppress the paired 10% rule, the sample/cache/RSS matrix is explicit, and overturn restores exact-OS plus the original runner classes. One accepted observability repair remains incomplete: the process-architecture recipe does not define a valid observation of the launched target process. On Linux, an inspecting `file /proc/self/exe` observes the inspector itself, not the target; on macOS, `file` of a universal running-image path describes available executable slices, not the slice selected by the target process. The bare `ps` alternative supplies neither a target PID nor a field/normalization rule, and an external `sysctl.proc_translated` query likewise needs target-process semantics. Because this leaves a SHOULD-FIX in the claimed fail-closed no-Rosetta proof, CONSENT and the proposed condition-4 MET transition are not available.

objections.title: The process-architecture and translation preflight still do not observe the target process
objections.finding: Preflight item 2 says process architecture is measured from the launched process, but its mechanisms do not make that statement executable. `/proc/self` is resolved for the process accessing procfs, so invoking `file /proc/self/exe` inspects the `file` process rather than the OpenSIP process. The unspecified `ps` branch identifies neither the captured target PID nor an architecture field and normalization. macOS `file` of the running image observes the executable file and, for a universal Mach-O, reports its available slices rather than which slice the launched target selected. Item 9 names `sysctl.proc_translated` without saying that the value must be obtained in the target process; running an external `sysctl` utility observes that utility's translation state, not necessarily the target's. Consequently the contract can accept an inspector that matches the class while the measured target runs under a different ABI or Rosetta.
evidence: D-098 turn 3 lines 133-138 specify `ps`/`file` of `/proc/self/exe` or macOS `file` of the running image but provide no target-PID capture, process architecture field, or normalized expected values.
D-098 turn 3 lines 153-155 require `sysctl.proc_translated` plus independent host/process facts, but do not define a target-process query; the independent process fact therefore remains ungrounded.

Linux procfs defines `/proc/self` as a link to the process accessing the filesystem and `/proc/<pid>/exe` as the target-specific executable link: https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v6.8/filesystems/proc.html .
The executable-architecture check already separately uses `file` and `lipo -info` at lines 133-135; repeating file inspection of the same macOS image does not establish the selected process slice.
objections.impact: The fail-closed preflight can record three nominally independent architecture facts while only proving host architecture and executable contents. That is insufficient to enforce D-006's native-process/no-silent-Rosetta obligation and leaves the proposed G03/G04 contract incomplete for condition-4 MET.
objections.requiredRepair: Define target-specific process observation end to end: capture and retain the exact launched target PID; on Linux inspect `/proc/<target-pid>/exe` and a target-specific ABI fact, or have the target self-report a normalized architecture; on macOS use a documented target-PID process-architecture observation or target self-report that identifies the selected Mach-O slice. Obtain Rosetta translation state from the target process rather than an unrelated `sysctl` utility. Specify exact fields, accepted normalized values per class, lifetime/race handling for short-lived help/version commands, and fail closed on absence or ambiguity. Keep host `uname`, executable `file`/`lipo`, process architecture, and target translation as distinct observations. As this is turn 3 of 3, repair requires the protocol's post-cycle route rather than a fourth turn.
